channel.description: Approved local stories in broadcast order

item.description: New York is offering one point five million dollars in grants to help communities conserve forests. Municipalities can use the funds to buy land or easements that protect wildlife habitat and provide public recreation. This supports the state's goal to conserve thirty percent of its lands and waters by two thousand thirty.

Vermont’s moose hunting season has ended with fewer permits issued this year. The hunt helps control moose numbers and reduce harmful winter ticks. Hunters face challenges hauling these large animals out of wildlife areas without motorized vehicles.

Lead contamination is found in drinking water at forty-two percent of New York schools. Adirondack counties like St. Lawrence and Lewis have some of the highest rates. Advocates urge stricter limits and filters to protect children’s health.

A tragic crash in Warren Vermont has claimed the life of a fourteen-year-old passenger. The sixteen-year-old driver suffered minor injuries and is recovering. The community and Harwood School District are mourning this loss and offering support.
